subject: Private VPC / Air-gapped: hardware upgrade window + fallback plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@genomex.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@genomex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Feb 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: on-prem / air-gapped post-call — proposed upgrade windows and fallback

Hi Priya / Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed path for the on-prem upgrade and the contingency plan if anything blocks the offline window. Attaching the diagram and the spare parts list mentioned on the call.

Key takeaways from our call:
- Scope: software upgrade + firmware microcode on two appliance racks in your QA cluster (rack-A, rack-B). No SAN changes expected.
- Constraints: air-gapped environment, signed package delivery only, on-site-only maintenance with Genomex ops present.
- Risk areas: unexpected firmware rollback, NVMe firmware compatibility on rack-B, and inventory of hot spares.

Proposed maintenance windows (pick one):
- Option A: Weekend window — Sat 03/09 00:00–06:00 PST (preferred for minimal traffic)
- Option B: Mid-week night — Wed 03/13 22:00–04:00 PST (if weekend is not possible)

Upgrade sequence (high-level):
1) Pre-checks and on-site inventory verification (30m)
2) Apply firmware to rack-B (staged), validate boot (90m)
3) Apply software package + KV cache warm-up to rack-A (60m)
4) Full integration smoke test (30–60m)
5) Roll forward / rollback decision window (30m)

Fallback options if offline upgrade cannot complete:
- Short-term: Fail over production traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool (we can pre-provision a reserved capacity slot) and keep your private VPC in passive mode until hands-on resolution.
- Long-term: Staged canary with incremental packages to reduce blast radius.

Action items / asks for Genomex:
- Confirm preferred window (A or B) by end of day Wednesday 02/22.
- Confirm on-site ops lead (name & contact) and access to hardware serials for spare ordering.
- Approve our plan to provision a temporary Dedicated slot for live failover if needed (we can include this in the MAP doc).

Attachments: genomex-dataflow-diagram.pdf, hw-spare-parts-list.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx

I’ve looped in Karthik for technical sequencing and Ben for the spare-parts procurement path.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@genomex.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: on-prem / air-gapped post-call — proposed upgrade windows and fallback

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock a window:

1) Firmware compatibility: rack-B has NVMe controllers running firmware v3.1.2. The vendor patch notes call out a compatibility check for v3.x — do you have a tested combination matrix we can reference?

2) Signed packages: we will only accept packages delivered on a signed USB and validated by our HSM. Can Redwood produce a SHA256 manifest and a GPG signature we can verify offline?

3) Failover latency: if we route traffic to a Dedicated pool, what's the expected 95th percentile tail latency difference for our current workload (~120 qps, avg tokens 45)? We need to set customer expectations.

Ops lead (looped): Marcus Silva (ops-lead@genomex.com) — Marcus will confirm serials and spare availability.

If you can answer 1–3, we can confirm Option A (weekend) or pick Option B if there's a scheduling conflict.

—Alex
Alex Moreno | Head of ML Ops, Genomex
alex.moreno@genomex.com | +1 617-555-0148
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@genomex.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@genomex.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: on-prem / air-gapped post-call — proposed upgrade windows and fallback

Hi Alex — quick answers below. I’ll also attach a short compatibility note internally (I can paste the matrix in a follow-up if helpful).

1) Firmware compatibility: We’ve validated firmware 3.1.2 on NVMe controllers for two of our customer sites with similar controllers; the main risk is a specific vendor microcode build dated before 2027-06-01. If your controllers show a build earlier than that, we recommend performing the NVMe microcode refresh first. I will send the compatibility matrix separately.

2) Signed packages: Yes — Redwood will produce a SHA256 manifest and a GPG signature for each package and include a secure audit trail. For air-gapped delivery we provide: (a) signed USB image (PKCS#7 envelope) and (b) an integrity manifest. Ops will validate via your HSM.

3) Failover latency delta: For the workload you described (120 qps, 45 avg tokens), expected 95th percentile latency increase when routing to Dedicated is ~25–35ms higher than on-prem appliances (typical RDW Dedicated profile on a c5d-equivalent pool). We can run a short performance sim to refine that number before the window.

Operational notes / recommendations:
- Window length: target 6 hours including validation — gives us a healthy safety margin.
- Sequence tweak: do NVMe microcode (rack-B) first, then software on rack-A. Keep one rack in passive mode for rollback.
- Offline package verification: provide checksum + signature + package timestamp; our field engineer will carry a signed manifest.

Ben will coordinate physical spares ordering with Marcus and Priya.

If everyone is aligned I recommend locking Option A (Sat 03/09) and taking the Dedicated failover slot as insurance.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Staff Engineer, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
